algorithm.Title: Finger Pain - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: UAT-only adult and pediatric non-traumatic finger-pain pathway screening for infection, constriction and neurovascular compromise before in-person assessment.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 for an ambulance for rapidly spreading infection with systemic illness, severe pain, a cold/pale/blue/numb finger, or rapid deterioration; do not self-drive. Remove rings if easy before swelling worsens; do not force them off. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Did this joint problem begin with a motor vehicle crash or as part of a multi-system crash injury?
questions.Information: A motor vehicle crash or multi-system crash injury belongs in the Motor Vehicle Accident pathway.

questions.Question: Is finger pain severe with a cold/pale/blue/numb digit or constricting ring, or is there rapidly spreading redness/swelling plus marked systemic illness or deterioration?
questions.Information: Threatened digit circulation, a constricting ring, or spreading infection with marked systemic deterioration requires emergency assessment.

questions.Question: With no emergency feature, is there any persistent or unexplained finger pain, swelling, wound/bite, movement limitation, child concern or higher-risk context?
questions.Information: In-person assessment is required to exclude infection, tendon-sheath disease, occult trauma, constriction and neurovascular problems.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency finger/hand response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 for an ambulance for rapidly spreading infection with systemic illness, severe pain, a cold/pale/blue/numb finger, or rapid deterioration; do not self-drive. Remove rings if easy before swelling worsens; do not force them off. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: increasing swelling or redness; fever or colour/sensation change.

advice.Title: In-person finger assessment
Content: Arrange in-person assessment for unexplained pain. Protect the finger and use wrapped cold briefly if comfortable; do not squeeze, puncture or use unapproved medication.
Call Back If: pain, swelling or redness worsens; fever develops.

references: NHS.UK, "Joint pain", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/joint-pain/ (page last reviewed 26 February 2026) - applied to non-traumatic finger pain
